_comment: Bitcoin Sentinel seed data — publicly documented suspicious addresses from law enforcement disclosures, academic research, and blockchain analytics reports. Sources include OFAC SDN list, FBI seizure affidavits, and peer-reviewed security publications.

clusters.name: WannaCry Ransomware 2017
clusters.description: Bitcoin wallets used by the WannaCry ransomware campaign (May 2017). Documented in US-CERT Alert TA17-132A and multiple academic studies.

clusters.name: Lazarus Group (DPRK)
clusters.description: Addresses attributed to the Lazarus Group (North Korean state-sponsored threat actor) per OFAC SDN List and US DOJ indictments.

clusters.name: Bitfinex Hack 2016
clusters.description: Addresses associated with the 2016 Bitfinex exchange hack (119,756 BTC stolen). Some funds recovered by DOJ in 2022.

clusters.name: CryptoLocker Ransomware
clusters.description: CryptoLocker ransomware payment infrastructure. Documented in FBI Operation Tovar (2014).

addresses.notes: CryptoLocker payment address — FBI Operation Tovar

clusters.name: Silk Road Darknet Market
clusters.description: Addresses associated with Silk Road. Ross Ulbricht convicted 2015; FBI seizure and DOJ forfeiture proceedings are public record.

clusters.name: AlphaBay Darknet Market
clusters.description: Addresses linked to AlphaBay darknet market. Shut down by law enforcement in July 2017 (Operation Bayonet).

clusters.name: ChipMixer Mixing Service
clusters.description: ChipMixer Bitcoin mixing service. Taken down by Europol/FBI in March 2023 (laundered ~$3.8B in BTC since 2017).

clusters.name: PlusToken Ponzi Scheme
clusters.description: PlusToken cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme (~$2B scam, China/Asia). Documented by Chainalysis and multiple court filings.

clusters.name: OneCoin Fraud
clusters.description: OneCoin fraud — one of the largest cryptocurrency scams (~$4B). Ruja Ignatova indicted 2019.

clusters.name: Known Exchange Hot Wallets
clusters.description: Publicly documented exchange hot wallet addresses used to reduce false positives. These addresses belong to regulated, custodial exchanges.
